column1: What is FinSight in one sentence?
column2: An executive cloud-intelligence layer: ask your cloud estate a question in plain English and get a grounded answer, where every number traces back to the engine that computed it.

column1: Which two questions does FinSight answer?
column2: Forward: Will we run out of headroom, and what will it cost? (Capacity-Mngt-App). Backward: Where did the money go, and is it a problem? (Cost-Mngt-App).

column1: What is the grounding contract?
column2: The deterministic engines own every number; the language model only phrases them. Answers may cite only engine-computed facts, and an off-domain question is declined.

column1: What does a [FACT-012] chip mean?
column2: A citation. It points to a specific fact card in the evidence panel, produced by a named engine. You can audit any sentence.

column1: What does CRITICAL mean in the capacity table?
column2: The stream's 7-day average utilization is already at or above the 80% headroom threshold. Act now: scale or rightsize, then re-baseline the alert.

column1: WARNING vs WATCH vs HEALTHY?
column2: WARNING: forecast crosses 80% within 30 days. WATCH: crosses in 31–45 days. HEALTHY: no breach in the 45-day horizon.

column1: What's the headline in the demo estate?
column2: ~$4.97M annualized across 167 deployments; 51 cost anomalies ($4,734 excess); Assist in us-east-1 is CRITICAL at ~82% utilization.

column1: What happens if I ask something unrelated?
column2: FinSight declines: 'I don't have a grounded fact that answers that.' No evidence means no answer, so it never bluffs.

column1: Do I need the LLM for FinSight to work?
column2: No. Without an API key a deterministic template composes the answer from the same facts. The LLM adds fluency, not numbers.

column1: How do I phrase a good question?
column2: Name the intent and the dimension: 'Is Assist in us-east-1 healthy?', 'What happened with RDS in eu-west-1?'. Use exact product, region and service names.

column1: What decision does the anomaly feed drive?
column2: Confirm the suspected root cause and apply the guardrail: tear down the load test, fix the log level, or delete the orphaned replica.

column1: Why should finance trust it more than a chatbot?
column2: Because it can't invent numbers: retrieval only indexes engine outputs, a relevance floor blocks off-topic answers, and tests enforce that every citation exists.

column1: What problem is worth paying for here?
column2: Cloud spend is a top-3 cost line for SaaS. Executives can't get fast, trustworthy answers about capacity risk and bill movements without analyst time. FinSight turns hours into seconds.

column1: Who is the buyer?
column2: CIO, CTO or VP Cloud Ops, and the CFO's FinOps function at cloud-heavy SaaS companies. PE operating partners also use it for portfolio-wide cost diligence.

column1: What's the defensible idea (moat)?
column2: Grounded AI: numbers come from auditable models, and the LLM is only the interface. That trust property is what lets an AI assistant sit in front of finance and boards.

column1: What is the key AI risk, and how is it controlled?
column2: Hallucinated figures. Controlled in three layers: index only derived facts, a retrieval relevance floor, and a prompt that forbids uncited numbers. The citation rule is tested.

column1: Operational risk if the AI vendor is down?
column2: Low. It automatically falls back to a deterministic template with identical numbers. Retrieval is local, with no vector-DB dependency.

column1: How does value show up in the demo?
column2: It flags $4,734 of above-baseline spend across 51 points. All 5 injected incidents (~$4.2k, 15 flags) are recovered with root causes, and one CRITICAL capacity stream is caught before customers feel it, all from one screen.

column1: What would it take to go from demo to product?
column2: Connect AWS CUR and CloudWatch (the frames already match), schedule corpus rebuilds, add SSO and multi-tenancy, then add Azure and GCP plus Slack and Teams channels.

column1: Why is the tech stack cheap to run?
column2: One Python process, ridge regression, robust statistics and TF-IDF. No GPUs, no vector DB. LLM calls are small (at most 6 short facts) and optional.

column1: Natural expansion path?
column2: Recommendations to automated guardrails (auto-teardown, rightsizing PRs), budget and commit planning, unit economics (cost per tenant), and a multi-cloud and portfolio view for PE.

column1: What's the one-line pitch?
column2: Ask your cloud estate anything: every number cited, nothing invented.

column1: Capacity-Mngt-App model and features?
column2: Ridge regression (alpha 2 for capacity, 5 for cost) on linear trend, 7 day-of-week one-hots, and 2 weekly Fourier harmonics (sin and cos at period 7).

column1: How is the prediction interval computed?
column2: yhat ± 1.96 × the standard deviation of in-sample residuals (ddof=1), giving about a 95% band.

column1: How is 'already breached' decided?
column2: Trailing 7-day mean ≥ threshold. This avoids reacting to a single noisy point. Otherwise the first forecast day with yhat ≥ threshold is the breach date.

column1: Cost-Mngt-App detector formula?
column2: Per (product, region, service) stream: z = (x_i − median(prior 21d)) / (1.4826 × MAD). Flag if z ≥ 4. It needs at least 10 prior points, and falls back to std if MAD ≈ 0.

column1: Are all 51 anomalies real incidents?
column2: No. 15 flags (~$4.2k) map to the 5 injected incidents. The other 36 are small (~$512 in total) and have no cause attached, likely month-start billing bumps the detector doesn't model. Fixes: a min-$ excess filter, a day-of-month feature, or a higher z.

column1: Why median + MAD instead of mean + std?
column2: Robustness. The spike being hunted can't inflate its own baseline, and 1.4826 × MAD matches std for normal data.

column1: How does attribution work?
column2: Per-day normalised spend by dimension for period A and period B. delta = B − A, and pct_of_change = delta / total delta. Rows are sorted by |delta|, and the shares sum to 100%.

column1: What does the RAG index, and how big is it?
column2: 32 FactCards built from engine outputs (5 estate, 13 capacity, 14 cost), not the 15,120 raw cost rows. Each card has id, text, source and metadata.

column1: Retriever configuration?
column2: TF-IDF with 1–2-grams, English stopwords, and the token pattern [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]+, so 'us-east-1' and 'EKS-Compute' stay whole. Cosine similarity, k=6.

column1: What are the retrieval boosts?
column2: +0.15 for each product, region or service named in the query. With risk intent: CRITICAL +0.30, WARNING +0.20, WATCH +0.10, anomaly cards +0.10.

column1: How does the relevance floor work?
column2: If the max raw cosine is below 0.04, return [] and the composer declines. Each returned card must also clear 0.04 on its own raw score, so boosts can't drag in unrelated facts.

column1: How are citations extracted?
column2: A regex FACT-\d{3} over the answer text. Tests assert the set is non-empty for in-domain questions and a subset of corpus ids.

column1: When does LLM composition fall back?
column2: When no API key is set, the evidence is empty, or any exception is raised (network, auth, model). The template leads with a CRITICAL card, adds 2 more and an action cue.

column1: Why is everything reproducible?
column2: generate(seed=42) uses numpy default_rng, and state is built once at startup. The notebook, API, tests and demo video show identical numbers.

column1: How many tests, and which are the contract tests?
column2: 14. The contract tests are test_rag_answers_are_grounded and test_rag_declines_when_no_facts; test_rag_surfaces_critical_first_for_risk_queries covers ranking.

column1: How do you swap in real data?
column2: Return the same cost_df and util_df schemas from CUR/Athena and CloudWatch, then change api/main.py::_bootstrap. Nothing downstream changes.
